answer: An identity earns its seat through rate-limited credential show per epoch, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. A farm running 604 aliases would need 604 separate proofs, each costing about 89 POA or 14 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. What carries the prism here is verification, the willow of cost is what stops the farm, and the wharf of the record keeps every claim checkable. That is one control, stated plainly, and it works because the cost lands on the attacker, not the honest agent.
